title: Token preprocessing operator fusion to reduce prefill overhead
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: The prefill (prompt preprocessing) stage is a significant contributor to end-to-end latency and CPU cost for short-to-medium prompts. Current pipeline runs several small passes (normalization, whitespace segmentation, subtoken mapping, and early KV-cache lookups) as discrete operators which creates friction: per-request scheduling overhead, repeated memory traversals, and poor vectorization. This is especially visible at high QPS for short prompts where compute per token is small but orchestration overhead dominates.

Goal: Implement an operator-fusion layer for token preprocessing that combines common steps into a small set of fused kernels (SIMD-friendly) and exposes a session-prefix aware microcache. Targets: reduce CPU cycles per token by ~30%, improve ingest throughput by ~1.5–2x for short prompts, and lower p95 prefill latency by ~10–15%.
proposal_summary: Introduce a preprocessing IR that expresses tokenization and early prefix-cache checks as a single fused operator. At runtime the fusion pass emits two execution modes: (1) a SIMD JIT kernel for hot codepaths (ASCII-dominant, short tokens) and (2) a safe scalar fallback for complex Unicode cases. Add a tiny session-prefix microcache keyed by (session_id, prefix-hash, model_variant) to short-circuit expensive normalization and subtoken mapping for repeated prefixes. Integrate with kernel selection so fused operators are preferred on GPU hosts that also run CPU-side preprocessing, and keep fallback heuristics when memory or CPU budgets are constrained.
design_notes:
- New preprocessing IR lives in runtime/preproc and exposes operator fusion hooks.
- Kernel generator will target AVX2/AVX512 and portable scalar code paths.
- Microcache limited to N entries per session with LRU eviction; entries store canonicalized byte ranges and token id slices.
- Fused operator semantics: normalize -> canonicalize whitespace -> char-to-subtoken-index map -> early KV membership check -> emit token ids + cache hints.
- Unicode correctness via property tests; we will validate against current tokenizer test corpus (unicode-corpus-v2).
- We will not change tokenizer vocabulary mapping; fusion only composes existing mapping steps to avoid model-compatibility risks.
implementation_plan:
1) Spec and IR prototype (week 1)
2) SIMD kernel microbench harness + scalar baseline (week 2)
3) Integrate microcache store and TTL/eviction (week 3)
4) Add selection policy and runtime flags (week 4)
5) Unit + fuzz tests; CI perf regression gates (week 5)
6) Internal canary across 10% of hosted traffic (week 6)
7) Full rollout with gradual scale after SLA verification (week 7)

Code locations: runtime/preproc/*, runtime/kernels/fused_*, runtime/bench/preproc_bench. Add benchmark scenarios to perf-dashboard: preproc-short-prompts and preproc-long-prompts.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end prefill CPU cycles/token reduced by >=25% on representative workload (measured in perf harness).
- p95 prefill latency decreased by >=10% on short-prompt cohort in canary traffic.
- No tokenization mismatches for canonical test corpus.
- Feature flag gating and fallback path present and documented.
- CI includes a perf benchmark that fails build if regression >5% on baseline.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Unicode edge-cases could change token boundaries -> Mitigate: keep scalar fallback and run exhaustive property tests plus customer prompt sample validation.
- Risk: Microcache coherence across scale could increase memory churn -> Mitigate: bounded per-session cache and metrics; opt-out for memory-sensitive Dedicated nodes.
- Risk: SIMD kernels may introduce subtle correctness bugs on different CPU microarchitectures -> Mitigate: per-arch CI jobs and conservative kernel feature detection at startup.
metrics:
- CPU cycles / token (baseline vs fused)
- Preproc p50/p95 latency (short prompt cohort)
- Throughput (tokens/s) for short prompts
- Cache hit rate and per-session memory usage
- Error rate (tokenization mismatch)
Targets: -30% cycles/token, 1.5–2x throughput on in-memory short prompts, p95 preproc -10% to -15%.
